name: Vectras Enprocon
summary: Vectras Enprocon is a Gujarat-based EPC contractor for the midstream and downstream oil and gas sector, building pipelines, combined stations and refinery and terminal piping works, and offering inspection and testing services. Revenue rose from ₹54.3 cr in FY24 to ₹119.8 cr in FY26 and profit grew 51.7% in FY26 to ₹15.4 cr, but operating cash flow was negative in each of the three years and borrowings grew much faster than revenue. The top 10 customers made up 92.3% of FY26 revenue, and the two selling promoters acquired their shares at an average of ₹4. At the upper band the post-issue P/E is about 13.0x on FY26 profit, below the median of the listed peers named in the RHP.

fh1.finding: Revenue rose from ₹54.3 cr (FY24) to ₹119.8 cr (FY26), a CAGR of about 48.5%.

fh2.finding: Revenue grew every year: ₹54.3 cr, ₹80.5 cr, ₹119.8 cr (FY24–FY26).

fh3.finding: Debt to equity was 0.59 in FY26 and 0.67 at September 2026.

fh4.finding: Borrowings rose more than fivefold (₹4.2 cr to ₹22.2 cr) while revenue rose 120% over FY24–FY26.

fh5.finding: Net worth rose every year: ₹12.2 cr, ₹22.3 cr, ₹37.8 cr (FY24–FY26).

fh6.finding: Operating cash flow was negative at -₹5.1 cr in FY26, against a profit of ₹15.4 cr.

pr1.finding: Profit after tax grew 51.7% in FY26, from ₹10.2 cr to ₹15.4 cr.

pr2.finding: Net margin improved from about 10.7% (FY24) to 12.6% (FY25) and 12.9% (FY26).

pr3.finding: Return on net worth was 51.4% in FY26, helped by the small equity base.

pr5.finding: FY26 PAT margin of 12.9% vs a peer median of about 9.1% (Pratham EPC 4.4%, Desco Infratech 13.8%).

va1.finding: Post-issue P/E of about 13.0x (₹200.1 cr market cap vs ₹15.4 cr FY26 profit) vs a peer median of 22.4x (Pratham EPC 34.5x, Likhitha 22.4x, Desco 8.4x).

va2.finding: Post-issue price to book of about 2.49x (₹200.1 cr vs ₹80.3 cr post-issue net worth) vs a peer median of about 2.13x, roughly 17% above.

va3.finding: Peer market cap to sales figures were not found in public sources.

va4.finding: No details of pre-IPO share issues or transfers were found in public sources.

pg1.finding: Promoters hold 73.49% after the issue, down from 100%.

pg2.finding: No information on pledged promoter shares was found.

pg3.finding: FY26 sales to related firm M/s Vectras were ₹17.1 cr, about 14% of revenue, with ₹11.8 cr of purchases from it.

pg4.finding: No information on regulatory action against promoters was found.

is1.finding: The offer for sale is ₹10.46 cr, about 19.7% of the ₹53.05 cr issue.

is2.finding: The issue is about 26.5% of the ₹200.1 cr post-issue market cap.

is3.finding: The two selling promoters' average acquisition cost is ₹4 per share, so the upper band is about 26x their cost.

up1.finding: No proceeds fund capex or expansion; ₹20 cr goes to working capital and ₹14 cr to debt repayment.

up2.finding: ₹14 cr, or about 32.9% of the ₹42.59 cr fresh issue, goes to repaying borrowings.

up3.finding: The general corporate purposes amount is not quantified in public sources.

up4.finding: Public sources don't say whose loans are being repaid.

lg1.finding: Litigation amounts were not found in public sources.

lg2.finding: No information on criminal or regulatory cases was found.

lg3.finding: The company reported no contingent liabilities at the balance-sheet date.

rk1.finding: The top 10 customers made up 92.3% of FY26 revenue, and the largest one 23.9%.

rk2.finding: The largest supplier made up 34.7% of FY26 purchases.

rk3.finding: The incorporation date was not found in public sources.

rk4.finding: Auditor remarks were not found in public sources.
